clusters.pattern: check_http_health: URL construction clobbered (url=None), AsyncClient timeout=None, client.get(None)
clusters.note: Tests stub httpx fully (mock get returns 200 regardless of URL) and never assert the url string or timeout propagation.

clusters.pattern: __init__ stores on_network_isolation=None / _handle_unhealthy gate and->or — entire network-isolation recovery path dead and untested
clusters.note: Zero test references to _on_network_isolation or check_network_isolation anywhere.

clusters.pattern: __init__ event deque maxlen=max_events -> None (history cap lost)
start: create_task(name=...) clobbered/omitted (NEM-5057 debug task name)
clusters.note: start/stop tests assert is_running only, never _task.get_name().

clusters.pattern: check_all_services: check_service_health(None)
clusters.note: Sole test patches check_service_health with a blanket return_value=True — None arg invisible.

clusters.pattern: run_health_check_cycle: docker args clobbered to None (get_container(None), get_container_status(None), _handle_stopped_container(None))
clusters.note: #12 raises inside the try (None.name) and is swallowed+logged; #5/#8 pass None to MagicMock. No test asserts the call arguments.

clusters.pattern: run_health_check_cycle: per-service 'continue' -> 'break' in grace-skip and stopped-container branches (cycle halts after first service)
clusters.note: Every cycle test registers exactly ONE service — multi-service skip/stop progression is never exercised.

clusters.pattern: run_health_check_cycle: recovery condition failure_count > 0 -> >= 0 / > 1; elif status != RUNNING -> == (healthy-path status promotion flipped)
clusters.note: No scenario: healthy + failure_count==0 + status!=RUNNING (kills #40/#16); no scenario: failure_count==1 (kills #17).

clusters.pattern: run_health_check_cycle recovery path: _record_event(service,'recovery',...) name/type clobbered (None, arg-swap, XX/case text on event_type)
clusters.note: Recovery tests assert only failure_count reset; event content never inspected.

clusters.pattern: All three _handle_* handlers + recovery: registry called with name=None (update_status(None)/increment_failures(None)) — silently no-ops for unknown names
clusters.note: registry.py:202 'if service:' guard makes name=None a silent no-op; tests call handlers directly with fixtures and never check the registry was actually mutated (only stopped/missing status on the handler-invoked fixture, which for #6 passes through un-noticed in the missing-container test — it asserts status only, not failure_count).

clusters.pattern: All three _handle_* handlers: _record_event(service,'failure',...) service/event_type args clobbered to None or swapped or case-changed
clusters.note: _record_event stores the clobbered values without error; zero tests touch the event history. Message-text-only variants are separated into the LOW-VALUE cluster.

clusters.pattern: _handle_stopped_container: on_health_change callback args clobbered, incl. boolean flip (service,False)->(service,True) and (None,False)
clusters.note: HIGH severity: #22 tells listeners a stopped container is healthy. The only callback-asserting tests route through _handle_unhealthy / recovery, never the stopped handler. The other 4 are arg-clobbers (real change, but a callback that ignores the payload wouldn't notice — still killed by an assert_awaited_once_with).

clusters.pattern: _handle_unhealthy: on_health_change(None, False) — unhealthy callback payload never asserted
clusters.note: test_callback_invoked_on_health_change_unhealthy asserts only call_args[1] is False, not the service arg.

clusters.pattern: _in_grace_period: elapsed < startup_grace_period -> <= (boundary-second off-by-one)
clusters.note: Existing grace tests use 10/30/60s vs grace 60 — never total_seconds()==grace exactly; distinguishing it needs a frozen clock.

clusters.pattern: _record_event: HealthEvent construction clobbered — event=None, timestamp/service/event_type=None, datetime.now(None), append(None)
clusters.note: HealthEvent is a plain @dataclass(slots=True) — no validation, all variants store silently. _health_events/get_recent_events have ZERO test references; get_recent_events also feeds system.py:1360.

clusters.pattern: _health_check_loop: asyncio.sleep(None) — check interval lost (busy-loop)
clusters.note: sleep(None) raises TypeError every cycle, is swallowed by the except, and the loop spins on the same TypeError path — tests only assert check_count>=1.

clusters.pattern: All _record_event call sites: message text-only changes (None-drop, XX-wrap, lowercase, UPPER) — HealthEvent.message is real stored data but tests never read it
clusters.note: Not EQUIVALENT: get_recent_events consumers (system.py:1360, health_service_registry.py:604) would see changed stored messages. But asserting event prose is canonical low-value; recommend mutmut exclusion rule instead.

clusters.pattern: __init__: log call cosmetic (message None/dropped/XX/case, extra dict None/renamed keys)
clusters.note: Pure log payload; no test or runtime consumer reads init log text/extra keys. (#21 verified via mutmut show: pure key-rename 'health_check_timeout'->'HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT'.)

clusters.pattern: start: log messages cosmetic (None/XX/case)
stop: log messages cosmetic
run_health_check_cycle: debug/info message cosmetics (skip-grace debug msg None, recovered info msg None)
_handle_missing_container: warning message None
_handle_stopped_container: warning message None
_handle_unhealthy: warning message None
_health_check_loop: log messages cosmetic (start/cancelled/stopped infos None/XX/case)
check_http_health/check_cmd_health: exception-path debug log message None (TypeError inside handler, but message-only payload change)
clusters.note: Strictly these would crash the exception path if the test asserted the return value — they survive because nothing asserts. Classified EQUIVALENT (pure message payload); flagged as borderline with LOW-VALUE.

clusters.pattern: __init__/stop: _task = None -> '' (both falsy, task slots behave identically)
_health_check_loop: break -> return in CancelledError handler (identical exit; only skips the trailing loop-stopped log line)
clusters.note: Verified via mutmut show; break is at the loop body's end followed by an out-of-loop logger.info.

drafted_tests.gist: get.assert_awaited_once_with('http://ai-llm:8091/health') + AsyncClient called with timeout=7.5; mutants pass None as URL/timeout -> assertion fails, original builds exactly that URL.
assert monitor._on_network_isolation is isolation_cb (kills __init__ #5=None); stub check_network_isolation True, assert callback awaited once with the real service and failure_count stays 0.
cmd-only service (health_endpoint=None) + isolation callback -> probe.assert_not_awaited() fails on the and->or mutant which calls check_network_isolation(None-name service).
event.service=='postgres', event.event_type=='failure', timestamp not None and tzinfo not None — kills all six _record_event field-clobbers; HealthEvent is a plain dataclass so no mutant raises.
max_events=3, record 10 events -> len(_health_events)==3; maxlen=None mutant yields 10.
_record_event spy: assert_called_once_with('ai-yolo26','recovery','Service recovered') kills T9 name/type clobbers; status==RUNNING kills update_status(None) (#19).

_handle_stopped_container with _record_event spy: exact (service,'failure','Container stopped') + failure_count==1 kills increment_failures(None) (#6) and the 6 stopped-handler event clobbers; same spy pattern repeated for missing/unhealthy handlers kills the other 12 T11 members.
failure_count==0, status UNHEALTHY, healthy check: status must become RUNNING (kills elif flip #40) and _record_event not called (kills #16 >=0 which records a bogus recovery).
failure_count==1 recovery: rec.assert_called_once_with(...) fails on #17 (>1 skips the recovery branch).
two services, first in grace: check_service_health must still run for the second — continue->break halts the cycle and never checks it.

two no-endpoint services, first 'exited': both statuses end correct (kills #13 continue->break, #12 handle_stopped(None) raises before status set) plus call-args set-equality on get_container/get_container_status ids kills #5/#8.
cb.assert_awaited_once_with(sample_service, False) — kills the critical bool flip (service,True) and all four arg-clobbers (#18/#19/#20/#21).
start() with _health_check_loop stubbed as AsyncMock (no timers/network); assert _task.get_name()=='health-monitor-orchestrator' kills name=None/omitted/XX/case.

freeze_time at restart+60s with startup_grace_period=60: _in_grace_period must be False (strict <); mutant <= returns True. Requires freezegun (dev dep — verify) and an absolute (not now()-relative) frozen clock.
